notes: Libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte (1787). Words follow the Schirmer vocal score's spelling and punctuation where the libretto differs: Anna sings "Il Padre, padre mio!", "tinto e coperto del color di morte" (libretto: dei color), "fredde le membra!" (libretto: fredde ha le membra), "Ora ch'è morte, o Dio!" (libretto: morto; the print's word is kept and its IPA is as printed, the meaning is the libretto's "now that he is dead"), "Tu sei perdon, mio bene," and "dov' è" with dov' on its own note; Ottavio sings "datele nuovi ajuti", "quell'oggetto d'orrore!" and, the second time, "La rimembrenza amara!" (print's spelling; IPA as sung, ri.memˈbran.tsa), and "vammi ondeggiando al cor" once in bar 154 where Anna sings "il cor". Lines are repeated as the score repeats them, each repeat its own phrase. IPA, word meanings and translations were drafted for this app (S04) and the IPA was checked against Castel. IPA follows sung Italian conventions: stressed syllable marked, elisions (two words on one note in the score) joined with ‿, open e/o as ɛ/ɔ. Translation literal, for meaning.

phrases.original: Ah! soccorrete amici, il mio tesoro!

phrases.translation: go and find, go and fetch me some salts, some cordial!

phrases.translation: Donna Anna! My bride! My dearest!

phrases.original: il duolo estremo la meschinella uccide!
phrases.translation: the poor girl is dying of such grief!

phrases.original: Celate, allontanate agli occhi suoi quell'oggetto d'orrore!
phrases.translation: Hide it, take that dreadful thing out of her sight!

phrases.translation: Now that he is dead, oh God,

phrases.translation: the one who gave me my life.
look at me just for a moment,
it is your own true love speaking,
It's you! Forgive me, my dearest,

phrases.original: Ah, il padre mio dov' è?
Lascia, o cara, la rimembranza amara!
phrases.translation: Put that bitter memory aside, my dear!

phrases.original: hai sposo e padre in me.
phrases.translation: in me you have a husband and a father.

phrases.original: Ah! il padre, il padre mio dov' è?

Ah, swear, if you are able,
I swear it, I swear it,
I swear it on your eyes,
I swear it on our love!
